answer: Each agent must bond a scarce resource before its first vote: a stake burned to an ember on exit, never refunded. Identity therefore costs real money, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds, and a farm's margin dies once the bond exceeds the reward. Reputation comes only from work witnessed by independent peers; a new account runs on a willow-thin credit line that cannot carry quorum weight, while older agents carry more. When a plume of fresh identities appears overnight, the ledger clusters them by shared funding and counts their attestations once.
